(i) the impacts of the push (GFC) and pull factors (domestic growth) on capital inflows vary substantially across the SDC, and (ii) FDI flows are basically driven by the pull factor, and their sensitivity to GFC does not appear to vary much across these thresholds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a number of important issues.
the impacts of the global financial conditions and the domestic growth on the capital inflows in emerging market and development economies.
the impacts of the push and pull factors on capital flows in emerging and developing countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impacts of the GFC and growth on capital inflows vary substantially depending on the SDC.
the domestic pull factor plays a key role in explaining the dynamics of all types of capital inflows and that the impact of GFC is substantially much higher in countries with better SCD.

, for emerging market and developing countries, the impact of domestic pull and global push factors on capital inflow is substantially higher for countries with higher governance and trade and de facto international integration and financial openness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impact of domestic pull factors is much stronger than that of GFC in determining capital inflows in countries with better SDRs.
the impacts of the push and pull factors on the main components of capital inflow are substantially higher for the countries with better SCD.
the impact of the main push factor on non FDI capital inflows is much higher in the episodes of better domestic governance, higher trade openness and higher de facto financial openness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the domestic pull factor plays a much more important role in determining capital inflows in the episodes of better SDC.
the impact of GFC is not invariant to the SDC and the pull factor is more important for the episodes of good domestic conditions.
countries that have been able to improve their domestic conditions are more likely to be able to withstand the impact of GFC and to be able to benefit more from the pull factor.
